simple.meaning: קְבוּרָה (qᵉbûwrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “sepulture ; (concretely) a sepulchre.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 35:20. The surrounding context includes family, family line, city, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְבוּרָה (H6900) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: קְבוּרָה (qᵉbûwrâh) / H6900 is traced through Genesis 35:20, Genesis 47:30, Deuteronomy 34:6, 1 Samuel 10:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

So Uzziah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.” Jotham his son reigned in his place.

If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial; I say, that a stillborn child is better than he:

He will be buried with the burial of a donkey,
